newsitem.title: USA: Video Update sees Q1 hurt by weak titles.
newsitem.headline: Video Update sees Q1 hurt by weak titles.

text.p: Video Update Inc said it expects operating results for its first fiscal quarter ending July 31 to be adversely impacted by the unpopularity of new video titles marketed during the period.

"Although we expect an increase in same store sales compared to last year's first quarter, we expect that our overall sales growth and earnings will be adversely impacted by the lack of public acceptance of new release video titles available during the period," said chief executive Daniel Potter.

"In particular our new superstores are not ramping up to their expected level of mature operations within the time frame we expected. We believe this is due primarily to the lack of strong new release titles available during the past two fiscal quarters," Potter said.

A lack of strong titles during the fourth fiscal quarter which ended April 30, may have discouraged customers from regular visits to their video store during the first quarter of fiscal year 1998, the company said.

"We expect that stronger titles will be available for upcoming quarters and that these will encourage customers to return to their video stores on a more regular basis. We expect that results for the remainder of the fiscal year will be enhanced by the availability of titles such as 'Liar Liar,' 'Dante's Peak' and 'The English Patient,'" said Potter.
Financial results for the quarter ending July 31 are expected to be announced during the second week of September, the company said.

Video Update has 393 video specialty stores in North America, of which 362 are company-owned and 31 are franchised as of July 29. The stores are located in 21 states in the United States and in six provinces in Canada.
